scenario: Adjudicating prior PARTIAL evidence (planet=Saturn, limit=10) — the MCP response itself showed several rows with mantra_sanskrit:null and mantra_text:null despite mantra_transliteration being populated for some. Checked whether this is a wiring bug or a genuine corpus-coverage gap.

db_verification.query_saturn_only: SELECT count(*) total, count(mantra_text) has_mantra_text, count(mantra_sanskrit) has_mantra_sanskrit, count(mantra_transliteration) has_translit FROM brahma_remedy_corpus WHERE remedy_type='mantra' AND planet ILIKE 'saturn'
db_verification.query_full_corpus: SELECT count(*) total, count(mantra_text) has_mantra_text, count(mantra_sanskrit) has_mantra_sanskrit FROM brahma_remedy_corpus WHERE remedy_type='mantra'

conclusion: The MCP response's nulls faithfully reflect real underlying data: only 16/67 (24%) of the whole mantra corpus has mantra_text populated and only 9/67 (13%) has mantra_sanskrit populated. This is NOT a wiring bug (unlike ref_nakshatra_get/ref_dasha_systems_get) — the tool correctly queries brahma_remedy_corpus and honestly returns null rather than fabricating text (consistent with CLAUDE.md N.7 item 6 'honest null beats invented judgment'). It IS a genuine, quantified corpus-completeness gap: for a tool whose entire purpose is 'mantra corpus query', most rows lack the actual mantra (Sanskrit or transliterated) and only carry prescription_text (contextual guidance/remedy instructions) plus classical_ref. Downgrades verdict to PARTIAL rather than a clean PASS.
